items.prompt: What does it mean for an event to "bubble"?

tests.description: resolves a click two levels deep to the correct button ancestor
tests.expr: let caught = null; const onClick = createDelegatedClickHandler('delete-btn', (n) => (caught = n)); const button = {className:'delete-btn', parent:null}; const icon = {className:'icon', parent:button}; const svgPath = {className:'svg-path', parent:icon}; onClick(svgPath); expect(caught).toBe(button)

items.explanation: A click nested two levels deep (like an SVG path inside an icon inside a button) is realistic in actual markup — this confirms the fix handles arbitrary nesting depth, not just the exact one-level case from the incident.

items.prompt: Implement `createDelegatedClickHandler(targetClassName, onMatch)` (same rules). Verify a NEW button (simulating one added to the page after the handler was created) still works correctly, demonstrating delegation covers future elements.

tests.description: a button created AFTER the handler still works correctly
tests.expr: const onClick = createDelegatedClickHandler('delete-btn', () => {}); let caught = null; const onClick2 = createDelegatedClickHandler('delete-btn', (n) => (caught = n)); const newButton = {className:'delete-btn', parent:null}; const newIcon = {className:'icon', parent:newButton}; onClick2(newIcon); expect(caught).toBe(newButton)

items.explanation: Since the handler's logic runs fresh on every call rather than depending on a fixed list of elements captured at creation time, a button object created afterward is resolved just as correctly as one that existed from the start.

items.prompt: Implement `closest(node, className)` (same rules). Verify it returns `null` when the node and none of its ancestors match, including when the chain ends at a node with `parent: null`.

tests.description: no match anywhere in the chain returns null
tests.expr: const grandparent = {className:'app', parent:null}; const parent = {className:'sidebar', parent:grandparent}; const child = {className:'widget', parent:parent}; expect(closest(child, 'delete-btn')).toBe(null)

items.explanation: Confirming closest() correctly returns null when it exhausts the entire ancestor chain without a match is just as important as confirming it finds a real match — a delegated handler relies on this to correctly ignore unrelated clicks.

items.prompt: Implement `naiveDelegatedHandler(targetClassName, onMatch)` (same rules). Verify it fails the same way for a click two levels deep (a grandchild of the target), not just one level deep.

tests.description: a click two levels deep also fails to trigger onMatch
tests.expr: let caught = null; const onClick = naiveDelegatedHandler('delete-btn', (n) => (caught = n)); const button = {className:'delete-btn', parent:null}; const icon = {className:'icon', parent:button}; const svgPath = {className:'svg-path', parent:icon}; onClick(svgPath); expect(caught).toBe(null)

items.explanation: The naive handler's flaw isn't limited to one level of nesting — any descendant, no matter how deeply nested, fails the direct check, which is exactly why real markup with icons-inside-spans-inside-buttons is especially prone to this bug.

items.prompt: Implement `createDelegatedClickHandler(targetClassName, onMatch)` (same rules). Verify it correctly handles two sibling buttons — clicking one sibling's icon never resolves to the other sibling's button.

tests.description: clicking one sibling's icon resolves to that sibling's own button, not the other
tests.expr: let caught = null; const onClick = createDelegatedClickHandler('delete-btn', (n) => (caught = n)); const buttonA = {className:'delete-btn', id:'A', parent:null}; const iconA = {className:'icon', parent:buttonA}; const buttonB = {className:'delete-btn', id:'B', parent:null}; onClick(iconA); expect(caught).toBe(buttonA); expect(caught === buttonB).toBe(false)

items.explanation: This confirms the fix correctly scopes to the specific clicked item's own ancestor chain — a real todo list has many sibling delete buttons, and the fix must never cross-resolve one item's icon to a different item's button.
